frozen_protocol.support: distinct positive training viewers per media
frozen_protocol.candidate_rule: available_from_utc <= cutoff_utc < available_to_utc; include eligible zero-history items

days.title: Define an observed signal without inventing preferences

engineering.practice: From already validated events, return distinct (viewer_id, media_id) pairs whose watch_seconds is greater than zero. Do not read files, aggregate holdout into training, or infer dislikes.

guidance.worked_example: One viewer watches d twice with different event IDs: one positive pair. A zero-second event contributes none. An unseen item is not a negative label.

acceptance: Repeated positive events for the same viewer/media collapse to one pair; different viewers remain distinct.
Zero-watch events are excluded; input events and order are not mutated.
The protocol is declared before inspecting aggregate holdout scores; no optimization of threshold or K.
engineering.evidence: Record exact command/result or named TODO, independent expected value/counterexample, assistance, one guarantee and one limit. No fabricated completion.
engineering.architecture_explanation: Use a pure projection over already validated events: keep distinct (viewer_id, media_id) pairs only when watch_seconds > 0. This keeps parsing and temporal split duties in earlier modules and avoids treating unseen items as dislikes. If the A/B gate is unmet, this day’s implementation slice recovers that gate first.

days.title: Count distinct positive training viewers

engineering.practice: Initialize every candidate score to zero; count distinct positive viewers from training pairs only. Use retained train events through positive_pairs, not the older event-count/watch-total summary.

guidance.worked_example: d has v1 twice, v2 and v3: support 3, not 4. b has v1, v2 and zero-watch v4: support 2. Expired x can have high historical support but cannot enter the candidate score map.

acceptance: Counts match literal hand-calculated distinct-viewer support and include zero-count candidates.
Changing otherwise-valid held-out events cannot change support.
Adding a new positive training viewer changes the appropriate support; a repeated existing pair does not.
engineering.evidence: Record exact command/result or named TODO, independent expected value/counterexample, assistance, one guarantee and one limit. No fabricated completion.
engineering.architecture_explanation: Initialize every eligible candidate at zero and count each distinct positive (viewer, media) pair once. Consume Day 169’s pair projection, not event counts or watch duration. If the A/B gate is unmet, use the implementation slice for gate recovery.

days.title: Produce one deterministic global top-three list

engineering.practice: Sort candidates by descending distinct-positive-viewer count, then exact media ID ascending; take at most three. The same list is used for every viewer, including already-seen items. Extra time goes to tie and short-list tests.

guidance.worked_example: Scores d=3, b=2, c=1, a=0 produce [d, b, c]. Equal scores must ignore input order. Two candidates produce two recommendations, not padded duplicates.

optional_lesson.use: optional existing-access conceptual alternative within the study cap

acceptance: Full order and top-three match the independent oracle; tied input permutations give identical order.
No duplicates, personalized seen-item filtering, random fallback, holdout input or adaptive K.
With no positive training signal, the tie-break is a visibly labeled ID-order fallback; with no candidates the list is empty.
engineering.evidence: Record exact command/result or named TODO, independent expected value/counterexample, assistance, one guarantee and one limit. No fabricated completion.
engineering.architecture_explanation: Sort one global candidate score map by support descending and exact media ID ascending; take at most K=3. The result does not depend on viewer history, holdout data, randomness, or adaptive K.

days.title: Build the evaluation cohort without deleting difficult targets

engineering.practice: Group distinct positive holdout pairs by viewer, while separately retaining all observed holdout viewer IDs and zero-positive viewer count. Do not intersect targets with candidate IDs.

guidance.worked_example: new has positive targets c and future item e: keep {c, e}. zero has only a zero-second event: count the viewer but do not invent a recall denominator.

acceptance: Repeated held-out viewer/media positives do not multiply targets.
Cold-start viewers and candidate-unreachable targets remain in the evaluable cohort.
No holdout and zero-positive holdout have distinct explicit statuses; all raw holdout viewers are accounted for.
engineering.evidence: Record exact command/result or named TODO, independent expected value/counterexample, assistance, one guarantee and one limit. No fabricated completion.
engineering.architecture_explanation: Group distinct positive holdout targets by viewer while separately retaining every observed viewer and zero-positive count. Do not intersect targets with candidates, because dropping unreachable positives would inflate recall.

days.title: Compute one viewer’s fixed-slot precision and recall

engineering.practice: Using supplied typed recommendation and target inputs, compute hits, positive-target count, Precision@3 = hits/3 and Recall@3 = hits/target_count. Keep the fixed-slot denominator even for a shorter list.

guidance.worked_example: Recommendations [b, a], positives {a, c}: one hit, Precision@3=1/3, Recall@3=1/2. Empty candidates with a positive target give zero, not NaN.

acceptance: Duplicate recommendations or more than three entries are rejected by the supplied boundary; no double-counted hit.
Empty targets produce explicit non-evaluable/null metrics, never a fabricated zero or perfect recall.
Literal fractions verify all-hit, all-miss, short-list and unreachable-target cases.
engineering.evidence: Record exact command/result or named TODO, independent expected value/counterexample, assistance, one guarantee and one limit. No fabricated completion.
engineering.architecture_explanation: Count each hit once; precision uses the fixed denominator 3 even for a short result, while recall divides by the distinct positive target count. Empty-target cases are explicitly non-evaluable.

days.title: Aggregate macro metrics with explicit coverage counts

engineering.practice: Apply the per-viewer scorer to every positive-target viewer and take unweighted means. Add explicit cohort/coverage counts, not new quality metrics. Cold-start means absent from all training interactions, including zero-watch interactions.

guidance.worked_example: Three recalls 1, 1, 1/2 give macro 5/6; three precisions 1/3, 2/3, 1/3 give 4/9. Seven raw held-out rows are not the denominator.

acceptance: Report all holdout viewers, evaluated viewers, zero-positive viewers, positive viewer-media pairs, candidate-unreachable pairs, cold-start evaluated viewers, candidate count and returned count.
No-positive cohort yields null averages with reason; positive cohort plus no candidates yields zero metrics.
A viewer with only zero-watch training events is seen, not cold-start. No difficult viewer is silently dropped.
engineering.evidence: Record exact command/result or named TODO, independent expected value/counterexample, assistance, one guarantee and one limit. No fabricated completion.
engineering.architecture_explanation: Reuse the per-viewer scorer, macro-average positive-target viewers without weighting, and publish cohort and reachability counts beside the metrics. Determine cold start from every training interaction, including zero-watch events.

days.title: Compare two predeclared baselines on the same cohort

engineering.practice: Evaluate popularity and the instructor-owned ID-order reference using identical candidates, targets, K and cohort. Report both metrics and signed deltas; do not choose a winner or tune on holdout.

guidance.worked_example: Toy popularity recall 5/6 versus reference 1/3 gives delta 1/2. Another fixture may favor the reference: preserve that result rather than changing the protocol.

acceptance: Both sides use the same cohort/config; a mismatched-cohort comparison is rejected or structurally impossible.
Undefined metrics produce null deltas; ties and negative deltas remain honest.
The favorable designed toy is arithmetic evidence, not real-world quality or causal improvement.
engineering.evidence: Record exact command/result or named TODO, independent expected value/counterexample, assistance, one guarantee and one limit. No fabricated completion.
engineering.architecture_explanation: Compare popularity and the fixed ascending-ID reference with identical candidates, targets, K, and cohort. Return both measurements and signed deltas; do not choose a winner or tune on holdout.
